relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist, and Kapoor's father, in whose song sequence the three-year-old walk-on appears.
relationship_to_romance: One half of the central romance; the 'Pyar Hua Iqrar Hua' duet that the child crosses is the romance's best-known scene.
character_gist: A country boy who walks to Bombay, is seduced by the fraudulent wealth of Sonachand's circle into life as a card-sharping '420', and turns back only when he finds the housing scheme is a swindle.
performance_recognition: The role is among the defining Raj Kapoor performances and the film among the biggest Hindi successes of the 1950s.

relationship_to_protagonist: The protagonist's love and conscience; no contact with the child walk-on.
relationship_to_romance: The whole of the central romance, and the figure the song Kapoor appears in belongs to.
character_gist: A poor, principled schoolteacher who loves Raj and keeps trying to pull him back from Sonachand's world, failing until the fraud exposes itself.

relationship_to_protagonist: The temptation set against the protagonist's better nature.
relationship_to_romance: The counter-pull to Vidya, and the reason the romance stalls for most of the film.
character_gist: The sultry society woman who draws Raj into the gambling and confidence-trick set, standing for everything Vidya is not.

relationship_to_protagonist: The businessman who makes the protagonist his instrument and finally shoots him.
relationship_to_romance: No direct part, beyond keeping Raj in the life Vidya refuses.
character_gist: A dishonest businessman whose Ponzi housing scheme promises the poor permanent homes for a hundred rupees, and who shoots Raj when he takes the bond papers back.

relationship_to_protagonist: The pavement vendor who shelters the protagonist when he first reaches the city.
relationship_to_romance: Part of the poor Bombay the romance is rooted in rather than of the courtship itself.
character_gist: The street vendor who feeds and houses Raj on his arrival, one of the film's images of the poor whom the housing fraud is aimed at.

relationship_to_protagonist: The adult form of the character Kapoor plays as a boy; the whole film is this Raju's last performance, recalled in flashback.
relationship_to_romance: Holds all three of the film's romances, of which the Mary chapter Kapoor appears in is the first.
character_gist: The clown Raju, performing for the last time after twenty years and summoning the three women he has loved, each sent a toy clown; his own father's trade and his mother's grief sit behind the choice.
performance_recognition: Raj Kapoor's most personal role, in a film that failed commercially on release and was later reclaimed as a landmark.

relationship_to_protagonist: The teacher the adolescent Raju loves, and the only person at the school who takes him seriously.
relationship_to_romance: The whole of the pairing recorded in Romances: an unrequited first love that she never treats as a romance at all.
character_gist: A new teacher who encourages Raju's ambitions and becomes the object of his first, overwhelming and entirely one-sided love; she marries David with Raju standing as best man.
performance_recognition: Remembered for the bathing-pool sequence and for the restraint with which the teacher's side of the attachment is played.

relationship_to_protagonist: The mother who raises the boy alone and withholds what his father did for a living.
relationship_to_romance: Opposes the ambition rather than the romance, and is the cost of Raju's choice.
character_gist: A poor widow who finally admits that Raju's father was a circus clown who died in an accident and 'gave her only tears', and is horrified when the boy resolves to become one.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man Mary marries, at whose wedding the boy stands as best man.
relationship_to_romance: Closes the unrequited first love, and returns the toy clown as the couple drive away.
character_gist: Mary's fiance and then husband, whose wedding ends the chapter Kapoor appears in and hands the boy's token back to him.

relationship_to_protagonist: The adult Raju's second love, in a chapter after the one Kapoor appears in.
relationship_to_romance: A separate romance from the schoolboy chapter, and outside the pairing recorded in Romances.
character_gist: The trapeze artist Raju loves and loses in the film's second chapter, performing as Meenu Master.

relationship_to_protagonist: The adult Raju's third love, in the chapter furthest from Kapoor's.
relationship_to_romance: The last of the three romances the frame narrative gathers.
character_gist: A Soviet State Circus performer whom Raju loves during the troupe's visit, and who returns to the Soviet Union.

relationship_to_protagonist: Raj's love from the moment she opens her grandmother's door, and the whole object of his revolt.
relationship_to_romance: The entirety of the central romance recorded in Romances.
character_gist: The granddaughter of Raj's old governess, daughter of a poor Goan Christian fisherman, who returns Raj's love, breaks it off once in jealousy over Nima, and goes through the elopement and the near-drowning before the fathers give way.
performance_recognition: Kapadia's debut at sixteen, which made her an immediate star and fixed the film's teenage-romance image.

relationship_to_protagonist: Raj's father, and the source of nearly all the opposition he faces.
relationship_to_romance: The principal external opposition: he despises the Braganzas' poverty and faith and tries to buy, bully and marry his son out of the attachment.
character_gist: A rich Hindu businessman with no time for his son, who treats the match as a social impossibility and sets Alka's family up as the alternative, relenting only at the near-drowning.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bobby's father, whose pride answers Ram Nath's contempt and keeps the two households apart.
relationship_to_romance: The second half of the family opposition, refusing the match from the poorer side.
character_gist: A poor Goan Christian fisherman, proud and quick-tempered, who will not have his daughter taken as a favour by the family that slighted his mother.

relationship_to_protagonist: Raj's former governess, the one adult who showed him affection, and the reason he goes to the Braganza house at all.
relationship_to_romance: The link that begins the romance: her slighted visit and her gift send Raj to the door Bobby opens.
character_gist: Raj's old governess and Bobby's grandmother, humiliated at the birthday party by Sushma and leaving in a hurry, which sets the whole story moving.

relationship_to_protagonist: Raj's mother, as inattentive as his father and the one who insults the governess.
relationship_to_romance: Supplies the slight that starts the romance and backs her husband's opposition to it.
character_gist: A socialite mother with no time for her son, whose cutting of Mrs. Braganza at the party is the film's first act of class contempt.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man the runaway couple fall in with, and the danger Raj has to get Bobby away from.
relationship_to_romance: Turns the elopement from a rebellion into a physical threat, forcing the climax.
character_gist: A criminal who takes the fleeing couple in hand under his own name, and whose designs on Bobby bring on the chase and the near-drowning.

relationship_to_protagonist: The bride Raj's father selects for him, and whom Raj refuses.
relationship_to_romance: The arranged alternative held against Bobby, and a rival only in the fathers' arrangements.
character_gist: The daughter of Mr. Sharma, offered to Raj as the socially correct match; the film treats her as her parents' instrument rather than a rival in feeling.

relationship_to_protagonist: His mother's dance partner, seen talking to Raj alone.
relationship_to_romance: The misunderstanding that makes Bobby break off the relationship and run to Kashmir; a rival only in Bobby's reading.
character_gist: Sushma's dance partner, whose private word with Raj at the party Bobby takes for a romance.

relationship_to_protagonist: Arjun's first love, lost to a marriage her father forces on her.
relationship_to_romance: The first of the two pairings in Romances, ended from outside and never reopened; Arjun later finds her working as a high-society call girl.
character_gist: The woman Arjun wants to marry, married off by her father to a man of his choice, and found again by Arjun on a business trip as a call girl in another city.

relationship_to_protagonist: His Christian college mate and second love, who goes with him to the hills and over the cliff.
relationship_to_romance: The second pairing in Romances, and the one the film ends on: she agrees when Arjun asks her to die with him.
character_gist: Arjun's Christian classmate, loved after Aarti is lost, opposed by her uncle and mother, and the one who answers his question on the hillside by jumping with him.

relationship_to_protagonist: The only person who sees Arjun's good qualities, the one he obeys, and the man he accidentally kills.
relationship_to_romance: Follows the couple to the hills to pacify Arjun, and his death is what turns their flight into a suicide.
character_gist: The schoolmaster who understands Arjun when the village has written him off, and who is pushed down the hill to his death in the scuffle that breaks the film's hero.

relationship_to_protagonist: Margaret's uncle, and an opponent of the second romance.
relationship_to_romance: Part of the family opposition that drives Arjun and Margaret to flee to the hills.
character_gist: Margaret's uncle, who with her mother refuses the match with Arjun.

relationship_to_protagonist: Arjun's mother, in the household the village reads him out of.
relationship_to_romance: No part in either courtship.
character_gist: Arjun's mother, credited in the family the film sets against his reputation as a bad character.

relationship_to_protagonist: The college authority over Arjun and Margaret.
relationship_to_romance: Institutional background to the college romance rather than a participant.
character_gist: The principal of the college where Arjun and Margaret are classmates.

relationship_to_protagonist: Raaja's love, who cannot tell him from his twin until the brother grows a moustache for her benefit.
relationship_to_romance: The whole of the pairing in Romances; they marry after the rescue.
character_gist: The woman Raaja courts through the film's twin confusion, kept at the edge of a rescue-and-revenge plot and married to him at the end.

relationship_to_protagonist: The bandit holding the brothers' sister, and the man whose henchmen kill Ram.
relationship_to_romance: Displaces the romance for most of the film by making revenge the business of the plot.
character_gist: A bandit who keeps the brothers' sister in his control and has Ram killed, and whom Raaja brings to justice disguised as his dead twin.

relationship_to_protagonist: Rani's father, the family authority over the courtship.
relationship_to_romance: The household the courtship has to satisfy.
character_gist: Rani's father, credited as the family standing behind the match.

relationship_to_protagonist: Raaja's companion in the comic register of the twin plot.
relationship_to_romance: Attends the courtship without driving it.
character_gist: Chander, the comic support around Raaja, credited with a friend of his own in the cast list.

relationship_to_protagonist: Credited as Parvati; the synopsis names the brothers' captive elder sister without naming the performer, so the identification is not certain.
relationship_to_romance: No part in the courtship.
character_gist: Credited as Parvati in a plot whose other woman is the elder sister the brothers believe dead and rescue fatally injured; the article does not say which part this is.

relationship_to_protagonist: A credited supporting presence around the twins' pursuit.
relationship_to_romance: No part in the courtship.
character_gist: Dayaram Divecha, credited in the supporting ranks of the rescue plot.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the two pranksters who make Ajay their target, then his closest ally through the murder investigation.
relationship_to_romance: The whole of the pairing in Romances, and a friendship-to-love built under suspicion of murder rather than in courtship.
character_gist: A college prankster who draws Ajay into the trio, decides with him to tell the police the truth, and spends the second half clearing them both while the real extortionist hunts them.

relationship_to_protagonist: The third of the trio and Ajay's friend, found dead before they can go to the police.
relationship_to_romance: Leaves Ajay and Nisha alone together, and his belongings supply the lead they follow.
character_gist: The slacker who with Nisha invents the fake extortion note, and whose murder turns the prank into a case the survivors have to solve.

relationship_to_protagonist: The investigating officer the pair turn to, and the extortionist they are actually running from.
relationship_to_romance: The external danger that pushes Ajay and Nisha together.
character_gist: A police inspector who is also Black Cobra, the real extortionist, using the investigation to close in on the witnesses.

relationship_to_protagonist: The club singer Ajay and Nisha seek out for what she knows about Vikram's death.
relationship_to_romance: No part in the romance; belongs to the investigation.
character_gist: A club singer named in Vikram's belongings, whose dressing room is the next step in the pair's search.

relationship_to_protagonist: The hostel authority over the students.
relationship_to_romance: Comic obstruction to college courtship rather than opposition to the pairing.
character_gist: The warden of the Shimla college, in the comic register of the student world the film opens in.

relationship_to_protagonist: A credited businessman in the plot the fake extortion note is aimed at.
relationship_to_romance: No part in the romance.
character_gist: Credited as a jewellery store owner; the synopsis's stingy seth, whose death makes the pranksters suspects, is not matched to a performer in the article.

relationship_to_protagonist: The band member Dev lives beside in drag and courts in a second disguise.
relationship_to_romance: The whole of the pairing in Romances, conducted entirely through two false identities.
character_gist: A singer in the girls' band bound for Kashmir, courted by an oil tycoon called Esso without knowing he is also the girl sharing her carriage; the pairing survives the unmasking.

relationship_to_protagonist: The second out-of-work musician, who witnesses the murder with Dev and hides in the same disguise.
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's parallel courtship, being wooed in drag by the band's manager.
character_gist: Dev's fellow musician, in drag as Salma for most of the film and pursued by Salma's admirer, in the comic mirror of the main deception.

relationship_to_protagonist: Attached to Dev's disguised companion rather than to Dev.
relationship_to_romance: The parallel comic romance that the article says also remains intact at the end.
character_gist: The man who falls in love with the 'girl' Salma and keeps the mistake going to the final reveal.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the villains who spot the two witnesses and force them into disguise.
relationship_to_romance: The reason the courtship has to be conducted under a false name at all.
character_gist: The criminal whose murder Dev and Salim witness, and whose pursuit keeps them in the band and in disguise.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the travelling company the fugitives join.
relationship_to_romance: Comic attendance on the courtship.
character_gist: Kanhaiyalal Chaturvedi, among the company met on the train to Kashmir.

relationship_to_protagonist: The band's manager, who admits the disguised men.
relationship_to_romance: Controls the proximity on which the courtship depends.
character_gist: The woman in charge of the girls' band, whose hiring of two new 'girls' makes the whole imposture possible.

relationship_to_protagonist: An old acquaintance whom Arun once talked out of suicide, and who finds him work when he leaves home.
relationship_to_romance: The second pairing in Romances, a friendship-to-love whose outcome the article leaves open.
character_gist: The daughter of hotel owner Diwan Pratap Chand, who repays the man who saved her life with a job at her father's hotel and becomes his second attachment.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Arun loves and is made to give up for his brother.
relationship_to_romance: The first pairing in Romances, ended by the father's demand rather than by anything between them.
character_gist: Arun's love, surrendered on his father's insistence that he sacrifice everything for the favoured twin.

relationship_to_protagonist: The father who openly prefers the other twin and demands Arun's renunciation.
relationship_to_romance: The whole of the external opposition to the first pairing.
character_gist: A war-disabled major on crutches who favours Kewal, alienates Arun, exacts the sacrifice of Rekha, and has kept from both sons that their mother is alive.

relationship_to_protagonist: Arun's twin and the favoured son, for whose sake the sacrifices are demanded.
relationship_to_romance: The beneficiary of the renunciation that ends the first pairing.
character_gist: The twin their father has a soft corner for, played by a look-alike performer, and the measure against which Arun is found wanting.

relationship_to_protagonist: Jyoti's father and Arun's employer after he leaves home.
relationship_to_romance: The household in which the second attachment forms.
character_gist: The hotel owner whose daughter brings Arun in as an employee, giving the disinherited son somewhere to stand.

relationship_to_protagonist: Credited in the family the film's secret concerns; the mother Arun learns is alive is not matched to a performer in the article.
relationship_to_romance: No part in either pairing.
character_gist: Credited as Parvati among the family whose buried history the hotel waiter's news reopens.

relationship_to_protagonist: The credited antagonist in the plot around the twins.
relationship_to_romance: No direct part in either pairing.
character_gist: Ghanshyam Thakur, the film's credited antagonist opposite the brothers.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist, and the former lover of Kapoor's mother; the older generation's story displaces the younger one Kapoor belongs to.
relationship_to_romance: Holds the film's principal romance, with Pooja, whose loss and reopening set the terms for everything the children do.
character_gist: A college poet who loses Pooja to an arranged marriage, gives up poetry for his father's quarry business, and meets her again twenty years later on her television show as a stranger.
performance_recognition: One of Bachchan's early non-action leads, in a film remembered for its Khayyam score.

relationship_to_protagonist: Vicky's mother, and the woman whose first love the film reopens.
relationship_to_romance: The centre of the older couple's romance, and the reason the younger romance stands in its shadow.
character_gist: Married to Vijay against her wishes after asking Amit to marry and keep writing, and twenty years later a television host who introduces her former lover to an audience.

relationship_to_protagonist: Vicky's father, the architect his mother was married to.
relationship_to_romance: The husband who works out what his wife's silence has cost, and whose generosity complicates rather than resolves it.
character_gist: An architect and admirer of Amit's poetry who gives his wife her former lover's first anthology on their wedding night, and later deduces why the poetry stopped.

relationship_to_protagonist: Kapoor's college friend and the woman he loves.
relationship_to_romance: The whole of the pairing in Romances, suspended while she goes looking for her birth mother.
character_gist: An adopted daughter who learns the fact of her adoption and leaves to find her birth mother, which turns the younger couple's romance into a wait on the older generation's secrets.

relationship_to_protagonist: Amit's wife, in the marriage Pooja asked him to make.
relationship_to_romance: The claim set against the reopened first love.
character_gist: Amit's wife, married under the promise Pooja extracted, and the person with most to lose when the old attachment resurfaces.

relationship_to_protagonist: Pinky's adoptive mother, and so the keeper of the fact that starts her search.
relationship_to_romance: Holds the secret whose disclosure suspends the younger romance.
character_gist: Pinky's adoptive mother, from whose household the question of the girl's parentage escapes.

relationship_to_protagonist: Pinky's adoptive father.
relationship_to_romance: Part of the family the younger romance has to be settled within.
character_gist: The doctor who adopted Pinky, credited opposite Simi Garewal as the parents she was raised by.

relationship_to_protagonist: The daughter of the last smuggler on Anup's list, courted while he closes on her father.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in Romances. Note the article's own synopsis instead has Anup wooing Sapna, Bakshi's assistant, for access to her employer, and does not describe a courtship of Seema; the discrepancy is unresolved in the sources located.
character_gist: Credited as Bakshi's daughter Seema, the romantic lead of a revenge film in which the hero's attachment is partly instrumental and is abandoned when he surrenders.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bakshi's assistant, whom the synopsis says Anup woos in order to get at her employer.
relationship_to_romance: Named by the article as the object of the instrumental courtship, which makes her the alternative reading of this film's romance.
character_gist: Bakshi's assistant, approached by Anup for her employer's details; the plot summary gives her the courtship that the filmography's romantic billing assigns to Seema.

relationship_to_protagonist: The last and most protected of the four men who killed Anup's father.
relationship_to_romance: The reason the courtship exists, and the man it is conducted against.
character_gist: The head of the smuggling group, with associates in New York, Madrid and Las Vegas, shot by Anup at the climax but surviving.

relationship_to_protagonist: The retired detective who shadows Anup across the film and to whom he finally surrenders.
relationship_to_romance: Supplies the ending that leaves the romance unresolved.
character_gist: A New York-based retired police detective and criminologist who follows the killings from country to country and is waiting at the end of them.

relationship_to_protagonist: Anup's father, decorated and then beaten to death in front of him.
relationship_to_romance: The motive that makes every relationship in the film instrumental.
character_gist: A Bombay police inspector honoured for his service and killed by four smugglers on Juhu Beach in front of his eight-year-old son.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the four killers, eliminated in Geneva.
relationship_to_romance: No part in the romance.
character_gist: Bakshi's associate Prem, one of the men Anup tracks down and kills abroad.

relationship_to_protagonist: A cameo as the protagonist's landlord.
relationship_to_romance: No part in the romance.
character_gist: A star cameo as Anup's landlord, paired with Hema Malini as the landlady.

relationship_to_protagonist: A cameo as the protagonist's landlady.
relationship_to_romance: No part in the romance.
character_gist: A star cameo as Anup's landlady, opposite Dharmendra's landlord.

relationship_to_protagonist: The love of a man living under three names, none of them his own.
relationship_to_romance: The whole of the pairing in Romances; the article closes on the question of whether he will begin a new life with her.
character_gist: The woman loved by the man raised as Kishan and sheltered as Ratan, and the stake in the article's closing question about whether his past will let him start again.

relationship_to_protagonist: His real father, unknown to him, whose courtroom success caused the kidnapping.
relationship_to_romance: No direct part; the plot's business is the stolen identity rather than the courtship.
character_gist: The prosecutor who sent Laxman Das's son to the gallows on the strength of his age, and whose own son Gopal was taken from a family function in reprisal.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man who kidnapped and raised him as an instrument of revenge, and who hunts him when he runs.
relationship_to_romance: The pursuit that keeps the romance unsettled to the last scene.
character_gist: The criminal who takes Dinanath's son, raises him in crime as Kishan, and intends to kill him at twenty-one, the age at which his own son was hanged.

relationship_to_protagonist: The doctor who treats him, disapproves of his life, and shelters him twice.
relationship_to_romance: Provides the household and the borrowed name under which a new life, and the romance, becomes thinkable.
character_gist: A doctor who urges Kishan to reform and takes him in when he flees, at the cost of letting his blind mother believe the fugitive is her dead son.

relationship_to_protagonist: The blind woman who mistakes him for her dead son Ratan, which is how he acquires the name.
relationship_to_romance: Her mistake supplies the identity in which the courtship is conducted.
character_gist: Dr. Anand's blind mother, whose grief for her son Ratan gives the fugitive a third name and a reason to keep it.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman he protects from the goon Nandu, and who then helps him escape.
relationship_to_romance: Enables the break with his criminal household that the romance depends on.
character_gist: Protected by Kishan in the scuffle that lands him in Dr. Anand's clinic, and the one who helps him run from Laxman Dada.

relationship_to_protagonist: The goon whose assault on Chamki starts the hero's break with his criminal world.
relationship_to_romance: No part in the romance.
character_gist: The goon Kishan fights off Chamki, the scuffle that first brings him to Dr. Anand's clinic.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Kapoor's guest walk-on has no contact with the story.
relationship_to_romance: Carries what romance the film has, alongside Helen's character, outside Kapoor's appearance.
character_gist: A con man who works the houses of the recently dead, selling holy books in their names, and is saddled with the orphaned Ginny on a journey to an Ooty orphanage.

relationship_to_protagonist: The child at the centre of the film Kapoor passes through.
relationship_to_romance: No part in any romance.
character_gist: A nine-year-old left alone by her mother's death in an accident, whom the villagers hand to a con man to deliver to an orphanage.

relationship_to_protagonist: The mother whose death sets the film's journey going.
relationship_to_romance: No part in any romance.
character_gist: Ginny's mother, killed in an accident before the journey begins, and the death Johnny learns of on one of his visits.

relationship_to_protagonist: The credited antagonist of the journey plot.
relationship_to_romance: No part in any romance.
character_gist: Credited as Gabbar Singh, with Imtiaz Khan as an inspector who is his brother, in the comic film's villain register.

relationship_to_protagonist: Attached to the protagonist rather than to Kapoor's walk-on.
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic interest, in a plot organised around the child.
character_gist: Johnny's girlfriend, credited in the comedy around the con man's reluctant guardianship.

relationship_to_protagonist: A star special appearance in the same register as Kapoor's guest role.
relationship_to_romance: No part in any romance.
character_gist: A special appearance as the inspector, one of a line of star walk-ons that includes Kapoor, Randhir Kapoor, Vinod Mehra and Rakesh Roshan.

relationship_to_protagonist: A star walk-on beside Kapoor's own, and his elder brother.
relationship_to_romance: No part in any romance.
character_gist: Credited as Dabbu, his own family nickname, in the film's row of guest appearances.

relationship_to_protagonist: The other half of a bond so literal that a blow to one draws blood from the other.
relationship_to_romance: The whole of the pairing in Romances, and the film's title role opposite Majnu.
character_gist: Born to the rival Sharwari clan, loved by Qais from childhood, kept from school for her reputation, married to a prince who cannot displace Majnu, and dead at the end with him.
performance_recognition: Kaur's breakthrough, in one of the most frequently filmed Laila-Majnu adaptations.

relationship_to_protagonist: The husband who holds Laila legally while Majnu holds her entirely.
relationship_to_romance: The rival the marriage installs, and the one who understands the lovers only when it is too late.
character_gist: The prince Laila is married to, who cannot take Majnu's place and whose late understanding of their love arrives after it can change nothing.

relationship_to_protagonist: Laila's hot-tempered brother, killed by Qais in revenge for his father, which earns the exile.
relationship_to_romance: Converts a clan feud into blood guilt and makes the separation permanent.
character_gist: Laila's brother, already at odds with Qais before either knows who the other is, and the killing of whom turns Qais into the exiled Majnu.

relationship_to_protagonist: The head of the rival clan, who stops his daughter's schooling and her life with Qais.
relationship_to_romance: The first and most sustained external opposition, acting for a clan rather than himself.
character_gist: Laila's father, who fears for her reputation when the bleeding-hand story spreads, takes her out of the madarsa, and with the Amari head agrees to separate the children.

relationship_to_protagonist: Qais's own clan head, party to the separation and the father whose death Qais avenges.
relationship_to_romance: The other half of the clan agreement that keeps the lovers apart.
character_gist: The head of the Amari clan, who conceives of the two families joined by blood rather than love, and in whose cause Qais kills Tabrez.

relationship_to_protagonist: A credited presence in the world the lovers meet secretly in.
relationship_to_romance: Attends the clandestine courtship rather than driving it.
character_gist: Zarina, credited among the women around Laila in the marketplace and town where the lovers meet again as adults.

relationship_to_protagonist: Laila's mother, in the household that confines her.
relationship_to_romance: Part of the family enclosure the romance is conducted against.
character_gist: Laila's mother, credited with her grandmother in the household that keeps her from Qais.

relationship_to_protagonist: The middle brother, raised Christian, and the trio's comic and dramatic centre of gravity.
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's most famous courtship, of Jenny, in parallel with Akbar's of Salma.
character_gist: Separated as a child while looking for food for the baby, raised by Father Gonsalves, and grown into a bootlegger whose courtship of Jenny and drunken mirror monologue became the film's signature.
performance_recognition: Won Bachchan the Filmfare Award for Best Actor and remains among his best-known performances.

relationship_to_protagonist: The eldest brother, raised Hindu as a policeman's son, and the law in a family of outlaws.
relationship_to_romance: Holds the third romance, with Lakshmi, the most sober of the three.
character_gist: The eldest son, knocked down by Robert's goons while chasing his father and adopted by Police Superintendent Khanna, who grows up to police the city his brothers work.

relationship_to_protagonist: Akbar's love, courted over her father's objections.
relationship_to_romance: The whole of the pairing in Romances, and the thread that gives Akbar his qawwalis.
character_gist: A doctor courted by the qawwal Akbar against the wishes of her father Taiyyab Ali, and professionally placed to matter in the plot's medical climax.
